One Net to Rule Them All.narr: This paper sits inside Domain randomization. The physical problem is that training and deployment are not the same world: the simulator, camera, robot body, or dataset leaves something out. The mathematical object is a distribution over simulator settings. Its concrete move: cross-platform randomization lets one net fly distinct quadcopters. That turns sim-to-real into this operation: sample many plausible worlds instead of trusting one guessed world.
One Net to Rule Them All.how:
What it operates on: simulated states, real observations, demonstrations, labels, parameters, or rendered scenes.

The operation: define a distribution over simulator settings; estimate it, sample it, align it, or filter it; then train the policy or perception model on the corrected object rather than on the raw mismatch.

Why the math helps: Reality is treated as one draw from a range. If training covers the real setting, the policy does not depend on a single fragile parameter value. This explains the transfer mechanism without relying on benchmark names or unsupported numbers.
